texts: Coraline Ash arrived in Aelmere in the late summer of Year 1.
Coraline Ash arrived two days before the autumn equinox.
Coraline Ash came on a market boat from a village down the coast.
Old Vesh and Coraline Ash met at the harbor.
Old Vesh walked with Coraline Ash to the Watch.

Coraline Ash arrived two days before the autumn equinox.

q1_issues.issue: Sentence 2 re-describes the same past arrival by Coraline Ash that sentence 1 introduced (late summer and two days before the autumn equinox are the same time), so Coreference & anaphora's rule to reuse the symbol for a later mention of an already-introduced event should have put (BeforeBy ... sk_equinox_1 2 day) on sk_arrive_1 instead of minting a duplicate arrive event.

q2_gaps: A non-deictic season anchored to a stated year ('in the late summer of Year 1'): the Time term list has no season constructor and the bare-symbol licence covers only speech-anchored deictic seasons (last_spring / next_summer), so 'late summer' has no licensed form and the modifier 'late' has no carrier of its own.

Event coreference by full-clause re-description rather than a pronoun: the instruction set states the principle (reuse the symbol for a later mention of an already-introduced event) but gives a mechanical test only for pronominal event anaphora ('it'/'this'/'that'), and Events says to mint a fresh sk_<verb>_<n> per verbal clause.
review.notes: Down, Instrument, CoAgent, the collective two-Agent 'met', the BeforeBy gap, the capitalized-run name old_vesh, and the no-Name treatment of 'the Watch' all follow the instruction set exactly. The three motion clauses (arrived / arrived / came) become three separate event witnesses; only the arrive/arrive pair is flagged, since 'came' is a different lemma and cross-lemma event identity is not addressed.

issues.reason: Events mandates a fresh sk_<verb>_<n> for each verbal clause and the Coreference section's only mechanical event case is pronominal event anaphora ('it'/'this'/'that' pointing at a clause), so identifying two independently asserted arrive clauses as one event is uncovered territory — every atom on sk_arrive_2 (arrive, Coraline Ash as Agent, Past, the two-day gap to the equinox) is true of sentence 2 and well-typed, and nothing in the parse asserts the two arrivals are distinct, so this is the reviewer's own second gap mistaken for a parse defect.

gaps_confirmed: A non-deictic season anchored to a stated year ('in the late summer of Year 1'): the Time term list has no season constructor and the bare-symbol licence covers only speech-anchored deictic seasons, so late_summer and its 'late' modifier have no licensed carrier.

Event coreference by full-clause re-description: the Coreference principle names events, but the only mechanical test given is pronominal event anaphora, while Events says to mint a fresh witness per verbal clause — the two give opposite answers here.
new_gaps: A conveyance PP ('came on a market boat'): the preposition 'on' cues the Location role by the in/at/on list, while a vehicle is a 'conduit' under Instrument's gloss, and no rule separates a conveyance/means from a venue — the same undecided boundary reaches any means-PP headed by a locative preposition.
adjudication.notes: The rest of the passage follows the instruction set closely: the equinox anchor gets only its class atom plus the BeforeBy gap, 'met' is the collective one-event two-Agent form, 'with Coraline Ash' is CoAgent, 'down the coast' keeps the entity-attached surface preposition, and 'the Watch' correctly takes no Name. If a later instruction set supplies a mechanical test for full-clause event re-description this record would merge sk_arrive_2 into sk_arrive_1, but as the instructions stand nothing false was emitted.
